title: Roos computation of derived limits of abelian groups
statement: Let $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathbf N)$ be the category of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system] of abelian groups and $\varprojlim:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathbf N)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ the inverse-limit functor. Then $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathbf N)$ is an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives and $\varprojlim$ is left exact additive, so its right derived functors $R^q\varprojlim$ are defined [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For an inverse system $(A_n,f_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n)$ of abelian groups let $1-s:\prod_nA_n\to\prod_nA_n$ be the map $(x_n)_n\mapsto(x_n-f_n(x_{n+1}))_n$. Then, naturally in $(A_n)$, $\varprojlim_nA_n=\ker(1-s)$, $R^1\varprojlim_nA_n\cong\operatorname{coker}(1-s)$, and $R^q\varprojlim_nA_n=0$ for every $q\geq2$.

proof.text: The tower category is abelian by the Mathlib functor-category instance. The already proved roosTowerEnoughInjectives supplies enough injectives; roosLimitAdditive proves additivity directly by composing with every projection. Finite-limit preservation of lim is inferred from Mathlib, since lim is a right adjoint.

Define roosInclusion by the limit projections into the product. Its composite with 1-s is zero by limit.w. The kernel projections satisfy the adjacent transition equations by kernel.condition; NatTrans.ofOpSequence makes them a cone. Define roosKernelIso using kernel.lift and limit.lift. Both inverse identities follow after composing with the limit or product projections; cancel the kernel inclusion for the kernel-side identity. For naturality cancel the kernel inclusion and use limMap_π and Pi.map_π. All these helpers are proved without sorry.

Apply the positive-degree computation to obtain simultaneous e1, its naturality, and higher vanishing. Use the constructed roosKernelIso for e0, combine its naturality with the same product-map square h, and package the two isomorphisms, naturality equations and vanishing with finite-limit preservation.
